answer.rationale: P99 latency spiked 5x within 2 hours of a release during settlement peak. memory_b1 established that rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike without customer impact. memory_b6 showed staged gating can catch regressions, but this one reached production—the release timing correlation is strong. Rollback is the fastest path to restore write latency under heavy settlement load and has demonstrated success in this system. Verifying memory_b1 confirms the rollback mechanism itself is reliable. Single-intervention constraint and write-heavy load during peak settlement make this lower-risk than capacity-add (slower effect) or failover (unnecessary if release is the fault). Circuit breaker and read-replica routing don't address write-path latency. Rollback preserves uncertainty about whether other factors contribute, but empirical evidence favors release as primary cause.
